tvCategories.Title: Category List
tvCategories.Main:
Tree list of categories in the current workspace. If "All Workspaces" is selected, workspaces are displayed as root categories, but snippets cannot be added to them.
Virtual categories "Recent" and "Frequently used": snippets cannot be added manually to these categories, only modified or deleted.
tvCategories.Expanded:
ALT+A - Add category
ALT+E - Edit category
ALT+D - Delete category

lvSnippets.Title: Snippet List
lvSnippets.Main: Flat list of snippets in the selected workspace.
lvSnippets.Expanded:
CTRL+A - Add snippet
CTRL+E - Edit snippet
CTRL+D - Delete snippet

lvTags.Title: Tag List
lvTags.Main: Displays a complete list of all tags in the database. For convenience, tags already assigned to the selected snippet are automatically pinned at the top of the list and highlighted in green.
lvTags.Expanded:
💡 Navigation and Hotkeys:
Double-click — instantly filter snippets by the selected tag.

CTRL+ALT+A — add a new tag.
CTRL+ALT+E — edit tag name.
CTRL+ALT+D — delete the selected tag from the database.

ebSearch.Title: Search Bar
ebSearch.Main:
Database snippet search bar. Search is performed by title, code, comments, and assigned tags.
Smart Full-Text Search (FTS5):
The engine automatically searches for parts of words inside the code (e.g., query List will find TList). Results are automatically sorted: the most relevant matches will always be at the top.

Special Operators:
  • "Exact phrase" - search for an exact match (in quotes).
  • word1 AND word2 - snippet must contain both words.
  • word1 OR word2 - snippet contains at least one of the words.
  • NOT word - exclude snippets with this word.
Search is case-insensitive.
ebSearch.Expanded:
Type a query while the search bar is focused, and it will be applied automatically.

Tag Management (Global):
CTRL+ALT+A - Add tag
CTRL+ALT+E - Edit tag
CTRL+ALT+D - Delete tag

mContent.Title: Snippet Text
mContent.Main:
Main input field for snippet code. Supports syntax highlighting and auto-completion for Linux Shell/Bash.
  • Macros: The built-in engine allows prompting the user for arguments, inserting pauses, awaiting confirmation, and more. Full syntax is available on the «Macros» tab.
  • Execution (Line breaks): Each new line is interpreted by the terminal as an ENTER key press (sending a command). Keep this in mind when writing multi-line scripts.
  • AI Assistant: Built-in integration with Yandex AI Studio for code generation and refactoring. It is recommended to set up and use «Agents» — they return concise, ready-to-use code without unnecessary reasoning. You can configure AI via the main menu.
  • Data Protection: Snippets are automatically checked for sensitive information (passwords, API keys, SSH tokens, DB connection strings). If threats are detected, saving will be blocked until you explicitly check the «Ignore checks» checkbox.
mContent.Expanded:
CTRL+I - Open AI Assistant prompt window.
CTRL+ALT+I - Open AI Settings window.

mComment.Title: Snippet Comment
mComment.Main:
Field for notes and explanations about the code. Describe what this snippet is for, what parameters it accepts, or what to pay special attention to.

💡 Tip: Comment text is actively indexed by the internal search, so a detailed description will help you find the necessary script much faster in the future.

lvAllTags.Title: Tag List
lvAllTags.Main: Select tags for the snippet. You can move them by double-clicking or simply dragging and dropping (Drag & Drop) between the lists. Multiple tag selection is supported using Ctrl or Shift.

lvHistory.Title: Generation History
lvHistory.Main:
All passwords created during the current session are saved here.
  • Preview: A single click will return the selected password to the main input field.
  • Quick Apply: A double click will apply the password and immediately close the window. If the generator was called via a global hotkey, the password will be automatically typed into your active window (e.g., terminal). Otherwise, it will simply be copied to the clipboard.
lvHistory.Expanded:
💡 Generator Hotkeys:
CTRL+G — launch from the main program window.
CTRL+ALT+G — global launch from anywhere in the system on top of other windows.

CheckListBox.Title: Exact values (Smart selection)
CheckListBox.Main: Click on the desired values to select them. You can click on the checkbox or directly on the text for convenience.
CheckListBox.Expanded:
Advanced selection:
  • Brush (Drag‑to‑Check): Click on a value, hold down the left mouse button and drag the cursor over adjacent items to quickly select (or deselect) an entire group.
  • Keyboard shortcuts (hold while clicking):
    • Ctrl + Click — forcibly check items.
    • Shift + Click — forcibly uncheck items.
    • Alt + Click — toggle (invert) the current selection state of an item.

mEpoch.Title: Log and Text Analyzer
mEpoch.Main: Paste any text, JSON, or system log here. The program will automatically find all timestamps (Unix Epoch) and standard dates.
mEpoch.Expanded:
💡 Smart recognition of Unix Time (seconds, milliseconds, and microseconds) is supported, as well as dates in ISO 8601, Apache/Nginx, Syslog, and local time formats.

All found matches are highlighted: light blue markers indicate background timestamps, bright yellow marks the active timestamp selected in the list.

Bookmark system for navigation:
  • Ctrl+B (or context menu item) — create or delete a bookmark on the current line.
  • CTRL+Alt+0..9 — hotkeys to set numbered bookmarks.
  • Ctrl+0..9 — instantly jump to the corresponding bookmark.
Right-click brings up a context menu with a 'Go to Bookmark' submenu, showing a dynamic list of all active bookmarks with line numbers and text previews.

lvParsed.Title: List of Found Dates
lvParsed.Main: Chronological list of all timestamps extracted from your text, with instant conversion to local time.
lvParsed.Expanded:
The 'Relative' column displays live time (e.g., '3 hours ago' or 'in 5 min'), which updates every second.
Clicking any row in the list instantly scrolls the text (log) to the corresponding line, highlights it with a yellow marker, and synchronizes the calendar for further work.

cbIPInput.Title: IP Address & Mask Input
cbIPInput.Main: Input field for IPv4 address and subnet parameters.
cbIPInput.Expanded:
Supported input formats:
• 192.168.1.50/24 (CIDR notation)
• 192.168.1.50 255.255.255.0 (IP and mask separated by space)
• 192.168.1.50 (mask is taken from the spin control on the right)

If an invalid address is entered, the text turns red.

seMask.Title: Subnet Prefix (CIDR)
seMask.Expanded:
Defines the number of fixed network bits.

Common prefix examples:
• /24 — 254 hosts (standard local network)
• /30 — 2 hosts (Point-to-Point router link)
• /32 — 1 host (single IP address)

ledNetworkAddress.Title: Network Address
ledNetworkAddress.Main: The first and base address of the subnet, acting as its identifier.
ledNetworkAddress.Expanded: This address cannot be assigned to a physical device or server. All host bits are set to zero.

ledHostRange.Title: Usable Host Range
ledHostRange.Main: The range of IP addresses that can be assigned to real devices.
ledHostRange.Expanded: Includes all addresses from the first host (Network + 1) to the last host (Broadcast - 1).

ledBroadcastAddress.Title: Broadcast Address
ledBroadcastAddress.Main: A special address used to send packets to all devices in the subnet.
ledBroadcastAddress.Expanded: Packets sent to this address are received by all nodes in the subnet. All host bits are set to one.

ledUsableHosts.Title: Total Usable Hosts
ledUsableHosts.Main: Number of IP addresses in the subnet available for allocation to hosts.
ledUsableHosts.Expanded:
Calculated as: (2 ^ (32 - N)) - 2, where N is the prefix length. Two addresses are reserved for Network and Broadcast.

Exception: /31 subnets provide 2 usable hosts (RFC 3021).

ledNetmask.Title: Subnet Mask (Netmask)
ledNetmask.Main: Subnet mask in traditional dotted-decimal format.
ledNetmask.Expanded: Used by network adapters to separate the network portion of the IP address from the host portion (e.g., 255.255.255.0 for /24).

ledWildcardMask.Title: Wildcard Mask
ledWildcardMask.Expanded:
Calculated by bitwise inversion of the subnet mask (255.255.255.255 - Netmask).

Widely used in firewall rules, Access Control Lists (ACLs) on Cisco, MikroTik devices, and OSPF configurations.

ledNetworkType.Title: Network Type
ledNetworkType.Main: IP address classification according to RFC standards.
ledNetworkType.Expanded:
Possible values:
• Private (RFC 1918) — isolated local IPs (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x)
• Public IP — globally routable Internet addresses
• Loopback — local host loopback interface (127.0.0.1)
• Link-Local (APIPA) — auto-assigned IPs when DHCP is unavailable (169.254.x)

ledBinaryView.Title: Binary View
ledBinaryView.Main: 32-bit binary representation of the IP address.
ledBinaryView.Expanded: The | delimiter visually separates the network bit portion from the host portion.

lvVLSM.Title: Subnet Table (VLSM)
lvVLSM.Main: This displays the list of subnets obtained after splitting the original network using the new mask.
lvVLSM.Expanded:
The table contains the following data for each generated subnet:
• Subnet: Network address and its prefix (e.g., 192.168.1.0/26).
• Host Range: Available IP addresses for device assignment (excluding network address and broadcast).
• Broadcast: Broadcast address of the subnet.
• Hosts: Number of usable (available) addresses.

Note: To prevent program freezes and memory overflow, a limit of 4096 subnets displayed at a time is enforced.
